personas.name: routine-persistent-cough-flexible-bronchoscopy-complete
personas.description: Well-formed routine referral: persistent cough despite treatment, flexible bronchoscopy requested (first-line), no haemoptysis or bleeding-risk factors, every completeness field present — expect usually-appropriate + routine + low risk + accept.

request.clinicalQuestion: Persistent cough for 8 weeks despite treatment — exclude endobronchial pathology.
request.relevantHistory: Ex-smoker (20 pack-years, stopped 5 years ago). No haemoptysis.

expected.anticoagulantAction: No anticoagulant or antiplatelet recorded; standard bleeding precautions apply.

firedRules.description: Requested flexible-bronchoscopy is the recommended procedure for "persistent-cough".
No escalation rule fired; urgency follows the requested tier (routine).
No bleeding or procedural risk factors recorded; pre-procedure risk is low.

personas.name: two-week-wait-suspected-lung-cancer-ebus-antiplatelet-moderate-risk
personas.description: Suspected lung cancer with a mediastinal mass on CT and unintentional weight loss: EBUS is the recommended (ideal) procedure for the suspected-lung-cancer indication, and the indication itself auto-escalates triage onto the NICE NG12 two-week-wait pathway regardless of the routine urgency requested; the weight loss independently would only escalate to urgent, so the more severe two-week-wait wins; clopidogrel forces moderate bleeding risk — expect usually-appropriate + two-week-wait + moderate risk + accept.

request.clinicalQuestion: CT shows a 3cm right upper lobe mass with mediastinal lymphadenopathy — tissue diagnosis and nodal staging required.
request.relevantHistory: Current smoker, 40 pack-years. Unintentional weight loss over 2 months.

symptoms.imagingFindings: CT chest: 3cm right upper lobe mass with ipsilateral mediastinal lymphadenopathy (station 7).

triage.notes: MDT discussed; EBUS requested for nodal staging.

expected.anticoagulantAction: Review the antiplatelet agent (Clopidogrel); aspirin may usually continue, but clopidogrel / dual therapy should be discussed before biopsy.

firedRules.description: Requested ebus is the recommended procedure for "suspected-lung-cancer".
Suspected lung cancer / lung mass on imaging — NICE NG12 two-week-wait pathway.
Patient on an antiplatelet agent — moderate bleeding risk.

flags.description: Request meets NICE NG12 suspected-cancer criteria.
flags.suggestedAction: Expedite onto the two-week-wait lung-cancer pathway.

personas.name: query-referrer-massive-haemoptysis-other-procedure-mismatch-anticoagulant-incomplete
personas.description: Massive haemoptysis on warfarin, phoned through from the emergency department: an 'other' procedure was requested even though flexible bronchoscopy is the recommended (and rigid/EBUS the plausible) procedure for the haemoptysis indication, a clear mismatch that forces appropriateness to usually-not-appropriate and the recommendation to query-referrer regardless of the massive haemoptysis independently forcing emergency triage; the anticoagulant forces high pre-procedure risk, and several administrative fields are not yet captured — expect usually-not-appropriate + emergency + high risk + query-referrer, completeness below 100.

request.relevantHistory: Coughing large volumes of fresh blood since this morning. On warfarin for atrial fibrillation.

symptoms.imagingFindings: CT chest pending; portable chest x-ray shows no obvious mass.

triage.notes: Phoned through from the emergency department; anaesthetics and ENT aware.

expected.anticoagulantAction: Withhold the anticoagulant (Warfarin) before the procedure per BTS bleeding-risk guidance; confirm the omission interval and any bridging plan with the responsible team.

firedRules.description: Requested other is not usually appropriate for "haemoptysis"; query the referrer.
Unexplained haemoptysis — NICE NG12 two-week-wait pathway (people aged 40+).
Patient on an anticoagulant — high bleeding risk for biopsy.
